claim: When a server writes a typed non-continuation (a stop reason plus a machine code), assert that a CLIENT renders it, because a stop-reason ledger no human surface displays is indistinguishable from having no ledger at all - and the docs will keep claiming it works, since the route half genuinely does.
because: kp's agent-refresh route built a four-branch typed reply (refreshed:false + reason + AGENT_BRIDGE_KEY_INVALID code), pinned it with route tests, and documented that the operator sees it. The only UI calling that route awaited the fetch and read nothing, so a dead 24h pairing key, an undispatched agent, an unchanged status and a real transition all rendered as the same non-event. Route tests, the doc and the code constant were all green; the ledger reached nobody.

claim: When a projection SUBSTITUTES a measured rate for one derived leg of a chain, assert the leg structurally exists (a distinct intermediate step, not merely an in-range index) before substituting, because index arithmetic that only avoids underflow will silently address the chain's own start and collapse the substitution to the measured rate alone.
because: kp's hire forecast rebuilt its offer-to-hire leg as (offerReached/firstReached) x observedAccept, taking the offer stage as funnel[length-2] under a length>=2 guard. On a two-column board (a legal saved axis: entry + terminal) that row IS the entry row, so the ratio is 1 and the projection became velocity x weeks x acceptRate - 72 projected hires where the real 10% conversion gives 12. The signal-floor gate (hasSignal) did not catch it: the cohort was real, only the leg was fictional.

claim: A TTL is not a bound: when expiry is only evaluated on read, cap the store and reclaim expired entries before evicting live ones - and never mark an absent optional key field with a printable sentinel when that field arrives from a URL, because a caller can simply send the sentinel and key onto the unfiltered entry.
because: kp's server-side memo checked expiresAt on get() and never deleted, so entries keyed on raw ?candidate / ?roleFamily params (open vocabularies, on a long-lived self-hosted process where maxDuration does not apply) were retained one payload each forever. The same builders marked 'no filter' with '*', so ?candidate=* computed the filtered result (empty) and stored it under the full-list key, serving an empty decision-records list for the TTL. Both fixes are in the shared core; the joiner the module already used (NUL) made the absent-marker unforgeable.

claim: A theme-parity gate must assert that a themed surface RESOLVES its colour at render time, not that a literal equals its light-theme token: a lockstep check makes a hardcoded palette look compliant while it ships one theme's drawing into the other.
because: kp's diagram renderer imported the JS colour mirror precisely so its literals would fall under the repo's lockstep gate, and the gate passed - but those constants are the light half by construction (the mirror exports a separate DARK object nothing forked on), so every architecture diagram painted a near-white box onto the dark canvas, in the shapes AND in the legend explaining them. The tell was a stroke byte-identical to the coral token. Fixed by painting var(--color-*) from the SVG presentation attributes, which an in-DOM SVG resolves per theme for free.

claim: A metric's SAMPLE must be the population its statistic was computed over, not the population it was selected from - and the publishable/certifiable gate must read that same number, because the two diverge silently wherever the statistic drops rows the selector kept.
because: kp's metric pack sampled time-to-hire with the hire count (9) while the median was computed only over hires carrying both timestamps and a non-negative duration (5). The floor is 8, so the buyer-facing artifact printed 'over 9 hires', status:measured and certifiable:true for a figure resting on five observations. The producer had already been fixed to return the true count and pinned by a test; nothing consumed it, so the divergence was visible in the payload and still published. The fix had to reach the basis PROSE too - a basis naming a bigger population than the statistic is the same claim one sentence further down.

claim: When building an owner-style agent (not a task executor), give it a responsibilities layer distinct from mechanics - standing obligations, decision rules, refusal rules, escalation rules, what good looks like and how it is measured for the thing it owns - because the llm-agent bundle covers memory, chaining, fleet and transport and nothing says what a responsible owner of a codebase or a hiring pipeline actually does, which is the layer between LLM training data (generic) and a project instruction file (specific).
because: kp/personas App-master program, 31 sweeps: integrity and mandate obedience solved, product sense absent - the agent never chose its own work because nothing told it what an owner is obliged to attend to. Filed as a lead, not authored: the first subject (codebase owner) should be extracted FROM the P1-P3 evidence in the W8-pre program, per the registry doctrine that knowledge is extracted from operated experience.

claim: When a config format lets a LATER declaration REPLACE an earlier one for the same rule (eslint flat config, and any last-writer-wins layering), a rule can be fully present in the config text and apply to nothing - so a liveness guard must read the RESOLVED effective config for a representative file per scope, never the config source, because a source-grep guard passes for exactly as long as the shadowing holds.
because: kp's eslint.config.mjs declared four design-token no-restricted-syntax selectors in its first block; a later block matching a strict superset of those files set the same rule with only its own selectors, so flat config replaced them and `npm run lint` had not seen a hardcoded color under app/ since. The config DOCUMENTS this exact trap beside another selector group ('Spread them into both') and every other group was restated correctly - a known, written-down hazard, still committed. Two documents pointed at each other about which gate held the law and neither did. Proved by probe rather than reasoned: a file carrying both a hex literal and an await-in-transaction reported only the transaction violations. Fixed, and guarded by a test that calls ESLint#calculateConfigForFile for eleven representative files and asserts each selector group is present in scope and absent in its exemptions - verified non-vacuous by re-introducing the shadowing (3 of 12 fail, naming the missing group and the block to spread it into). The distinguishing detail: the population of hex violations was ZERO the whole time the gate was dead, so no symptom, no finding count, no drift - the only observable was the resolved config.
